title: A Next static export served from S3
readWhen: reaching for a server feature — `headers()`, cookies, a proxy, a route handler — or wondering why this is Next rather than Vite
summary: Next.js with `output: 'export'`. `next build` writes HTML, JavaScript and CSS into `apps/myself-app/out`, and that directory is the whole deployment.

title: A static adapter behind entifix's repository port
readWhen: loading content, or tempted to import `@entifix/testing-unit` outside a spec
summary:
A read-only static adapter, written in this repository, implementing the public `EntityRepository` port.
`get` / `load` with the Mongo adapter's filter, sort and paging semantics, including array membership for `in` / `nin`.
`save` / `delete` fail with a typed `EntifixLogicError`.
Records arrive as JSON and are validated from each entity's metadata before they are served; a failure fails `next build`.
Links resolve through `EntityLinkResolverTag`.

title: Pages render at build; interactive parts query in the browser
readWhen: a component needs data, or a page's client bundle grew
summary:
A — static content is loaded at build time.
C — interactive parts load in the browser.
C is where a backend slots in later.

title: An Nx workspace: app, domain, static adapter, content
readWhen: adding a package or an import between two, or putting an entity class somewhere
summary:
The adapter knows no entity.
Content is its own package.
Boundaries are enforced by `nx.tags` and `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`, replacing the old app's per-folder `no-restricted-imports` lists (#18).

title: English and Spanish, with localized content fields
readWhen: adding copy or content, or when a translation is missing
summary:
`en` and `es`, `en` by default.
Routes carry the locale.
UI copy lives in catalogs, and a key present in one locale only fails the build (#17).
Content uses localized fields.
The page picks the language.

title: Tailwind v4 and everything `@entifix/style` involves
readWhen: styling anything, or when a primitive renders unstyled
summary:
Tailwind v4, CSS-first, with `@entifix/style/tokens.css` and its palette presets, each scoped to `[data-theme]` on `<html>`.
Layout and atoms come from `@entifix/react-controls/primitives`.
The main barrel of `@entifix/react-controls` is never imported.
`./primitives` goes through `optimizePackageImports`.
The theme is applied before first paint.

title: Hosting is deferred; the build stays host-neutral
readWhen: a URL works in `next dev` but not in the export, or when choosing where the site is served from
summary:
`trailingSlash: true`, so `/en/cv` is written as `en/cv/index.html`.
A `404.html` at the root of the export.
Served from the domain root.
No redirects or rewrites.
`/` redirects in the page.

title: A landing page of five static sections
readWhen: adding or reordering a landing section, or when the in-page nav or the language switch loses its place
summary:
Five sections, in this order: hero, about, projects, entifix, contact.
The hero is typography-led, and does not move.
The section nav is anchors first.
The language switch keeps the section only when scripting is on.
Headings are copy, facts are content.

title: The radar's maths is ported, and it runs at build time
readWhen: the radar's blips moved between two builds, or a radar library is proposed
summary:
The geometry and layout are ported to TypeScript, and they run during `next build`.
The port lives in the incubator's radar control.
The radar ships no JavaScript.
The force simulation is not ported.
The control knows no semantics.

title: Content is checked from entity metadata, and every package ships `dist`
readWhen: a record fails `next build`, a member should be translated, a filter over a list matches nothing, or a package's code reaches the app as source
summary:
Validation reads `describeEntityColumns` — the resolved metadata, every default applied — and nothing else about an entity.
Localized members are a list beside the classes.
Rules the metadata cannot express are registered by the app.
No localized or collection member is `filterable` or `sortable`.
The read half of the contract is re-created.

title: A moving hero, a revealing nav and a blue theme
readWhen: the hero's motion or the nav's reveal misbehaves with scripting off or reduced motion, a first visit paints a theme you did not expect, or a printed CV comes out dark
summary:
The hero moves, in CSS only.
The hero shows no tagline.
Reduced motion turns every animation off.
One navigation bar. The section anchors (about, projects, entifix, contact), the CV, the radar, a language menu and a theme menu share one bar.
Language and theme are dropdowns, on native `<details>`.

title: The CV as a paper sheet, in variants and two modes
readWhen: a CV page spills onto a second page, an applicant tracking system reads the PDF wrong, a variant shows the wrong bullets, a CV URL 404s under `serve-out`, or the printed sheet differs from the screen
summary:
Variants. A `CvVariant` is a reading of the same career: its title and summary, the technologies it lists, the employments it shows, and the _focuses_ it takes.
Focuses select the bullets.
The sheet adds education, certificates and a location.
Two modes, both static.
Neither mode uses two columns, a photo, skill bars, or text in a header or footer.

title: CloudFront over a private bucket, defined in Pulumi, released on every merge
readWhen: a URL answers differently on `herbercolop.dev` than under `serve-out`, a deploy shipped stale HTML, a merge to `main` did not deploy, or an infrastructure change is being made by hand in the console
summary:
CloudFront in front of a private S3 bucket.
A CloudFront Function on viewer request.
An ACM certificate for the apex and `www`, validated by DNS in the existing hosted zone.
Cache-Control is set per object at upload.
The domain and its hosted zone are not in the stack.

title: A personal radar: rings for one person, editions in content, filtering over placed blips
readWhen: a blip shows the wrong movement, a ring's meaning is questioned, a technology needs its own page, or the radar's filter is about to query in the browser
summary:
Rings, for one person.
Quadrants stay Thoughtworks' four.
Movement is measured against an edition in content.
A static page per technology.
Filtering dims blips the build already placed.

title: Customizing the CV in the browser: the URL holds what is hidden, a stylesheet hides it
readWhen: a customized CV flashes its hidden parts on load, loses a choice on reload, in print or after switching reading, or the customizer is about to query content in the browser
summary:
The server renders everything; a stylesheet hides.
The URL holds the choices.
Hidden before the first paint.
The controls are plain props.
Human sheet only. The ATS pages carry no parts, no script and no controls: what a parser reads stays exactly what was built.

title: entifix queries run in the browser too: one use case, two repositories
readWhen: a filter or a list in the browser needs data, a page's scripts grew past its budget, a filtered view disagrees with the page it filters, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
The same use case answers a page and a filter.
The query string declares its parameters.
The static HTML stays the unfiltered page.
Two filtering rules are Mongo's, in the static adapter.
An incubator layer holds what is meant for entifix.

title: A blog of Markdown posts on entities
readWhen: adding or editing a post, a post fails `next build`, a draft appears in the export, a post's image or link breaks, or the blog's filter shows the wrong posts
summary:
A post is an entity.
Bodies are Markdown files beside the records.
Markdown with directives, not MDX.
Images and links are checked at build.
Drafts are for `next dev`.

title: The incubator owns content mechanics; the app declares sources and rules
readWhen: a loader builds an id → record map or casts a link, a new entity needs a source, a content rule is about to be written by hand, a page's filter is about to be wired again, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
Content is defined once, in the incubator.
Link targets come from metadata.
A load resolves the links it is asked to.
Generic rules are factories.
A source's published view is typed.

title: Layered packages: domain, content, entifix-incubator, implementation
readWhen: a file is about to be added and it is not obvious which package it belongs in, a component is about to load content or read a site class it does not own, a page's filter needs its data, a boundary lint error names `layer:implementation`, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
Packages are grouped by layer, and named from their folders.
The domain holds the business: entities, use cases, rules.
The implementation layer wires the domain to a delivery mechanism, in two kinds that never import each other.
What a component may reach depends on its level.
A filter's data arrives through a context.

title: Project pages, and decision records as content
readWhen: a record in `docs/adr` changed and the site still shows the old one, the conventions spec says the ADR copies drift, a project's page is about to show something its repository does not have, a record fails `next build`, or a Spanish reader asks why the records are in English
summary:
A featured project has a page.
Records are content. `ArchitectureDecision` is an entity (#77); `tools/sync-adrs.mjs` copies each repository's `docs/adr` into `packages/content/src/adrs.json`…
This repository's copies cannot drift.
Records stay in English.
The file tree is written by hand.

title: A changelog committed by the release
readWhen: `CHANGELOG.md` is missing a release or disagrees with its GitHub Release, the release job cannot push to `main`, a deploy shipped a commit that is not the squash commit, or `main` gained a `chore: release` commit nobody wrote
summary:
The release writes `CHANGELOG.md`.
A GitHub App pushes it.
The deploy ships the release commit.
`[skip ci]` keeps the commit from deploying twice.

title: A project's architecture and layers, drawn from content
readWhen: a project's Architecture or Structure section shows a part, a line, a step or a package its repository does not have, a scenario lights a line the hexagon does not draw, a package's box has an empty panel, `next build` fails on `architecture-nodes.json`, `scenario-steps.json` or `layer-packages.json`, a project page throws "Entity not found", or someone asks why a project's file tree is gone
summary:
Two sections replace the file tree.
Both are content. Seven entities: `ArchitectureRuntime`, `ArchitectureNode` (its ring, its angle, its `connects`), `ArchitectureScenario` and `ScenarioStep`…
The folders stay `ProjectPath`s.
An optional link is read by its id.
The drawings are the incubator's.

title: The delivery pipeline, drawn on the project page
readWhen: a workflow in `.github/workflows` or a git hook gained, lost or rewired a job and the conventions spec fails on "the pipeline drawn on the project page", the project page's Delivery section shows a job the repository does not run, the release decision on it disagrees with what a release did, or someone asks where the page gets the current version
summary:
A Delivery section on the project page.
The jobs are content, held to the files.
The graph draws only arrows no longer path implies.
The release decision reads the release's own config.

title: Content is read through entifix's ports, not the static adapter
readWhen: a use case is about to take the static adapter's types, content is about to come from somewhere other than the JSON files, `loadAll` asks a repository for a page of `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` records, a filter in the browser answers differently from the page it filters, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
The domain reads content through a `ContentReader`.
The static adapter serves repositories, not reads.
`implementation/adapters` composes the two.
An unpaged load pages.
Every repository is held to entifix's read contract.

title: entifix 0.23 takes the content mechanics back
readWhen: a record fails `next build` with `InvalidRecords`, a member should be translated, a data file carries a member or a record it should not, an entifix bump fails `pnpm install` on a patch, a page ships Effect it did not before, a header menu opens under the CV's toolbar, or code is about to move into entifix
summary:
The metadata says what a record must hold.
What the browser's copy carries is a view on the entity.
The static adapter keeps only composition.
The site declares its locales.
A patch is a pinned, named exception.

title: The tier contract, and the seam a host configures across
readWhen: adding a package, adding a dependency between two, deciding whether something is public API, or about to bake a host's value into framework code — a downward edge can still be illegal, and the seam takes values rather than paths
summary:
`i18n` is T2, not T0.
`testing-*` is T5, above everything.
A downward edge can still be illegal.
The subpath is not decoration — it is the part that works.
An exemption is named one at a time, with its reason on the line.

title: entifix is MIT, and the trigger that would freeze that choice
readWhen: publishing a package, accepting an outside contribution, or wondering whether the licence can still be changed — a shipped version's grant is permanent, the project's licence going forward is not
summary:
entifix is MIT. It is the simplest licence that makes the project open source, it is what the manifest already claimed, and every external dependency in the…
§3, an express patent grant.
§6, an explicit trademark withholding.
That ends with the first outside contribution.

title: Releasing without a credential, and the version a commit is allowed to cut
readWhen: cutting a release, wondering why the release workflow cannot be renamed, or why a merge did not publish anything — the version is derived from commit messages and nothing in this repository can publish to npm
summary:
Nothing in this repository can publish to npm.
`.github/workflows/release.yml` cannot be renamed.
A release is a pull request.
The branch is named for the version, so a version change opens a second pull request.
Publishing waits for a person.

title: The examples are the composability proof, and one of them gates every pull request
readWhen: adding an example, adding an e2e journey, putting an entity class inside a Next application, or wondering why a verb declared with `@useCase()` never appears on screen — entity classes need SWC's 2022-03 decorators, which Next's own compiler cannot provide
summary:
Turbopack panics in its decorator transform — `not implemented: ClassMember::PrivateProp` — on the `#field` every entity declares, and reports it as `Module…
webpack (`next build --webpack`) does not parse the decorator at all: `Expression expected` at `@entity(`.
That package is `sideEffects: true`, and it has to be.

title: Content an entity describes: locales from the host, a localized type, constraints, views, and one record check
readWhen: declaring locales, holding text in several languages, writing a validation rule a consumer keeps repeating, publishing an entity narrower than it is stored, serving records that arrive as JSON, or about to write a second in-memory filter — the host declares its locales, a localized member is queried one locale at a time, and untyped records go through `validateRecords` before anything serves them
summary:
Locales are a host value.
A localized member is one value with a text per locale, queried one locale at a time.
Constraints live in metadata.
Untyped records go through one check, in core.
A view is the shape an entity is published in.

title: A package's public contract is entities, use cases and ports
readWhen: adding an export to a package's `.` entry, adding an option that takes a function or an adapter's product, adding a requirement to a port's `R` channel, or a consumer cannot write an import ban because a mechanism shares an entry point with a contract — a contract surface never makes its caller construct a mechanism, and the subpath is what a ban can name
summary:
A subpath is required even when it adds no dependency.
A port's requirements are its own.
An option takes a port, or a key resolved at composition — never a function built from an adapter.

title: The host supplies the role ladder; the screen taxonomy is entifix's
readWhen: adding a role, changing who may assign whom, building a second host on `@entifix/authz`, or about to add a fifth screen type — the ladder's rungs are the host's and only the rule over them is the framework's, while the four screen types are the framework's own back-office model
summary:
Order is rank. A tuple says it once; a rank table beside a list said it twice and could disagree with itself.
An empty ladder and a duplicate rung throw at definition.
The rule does not move.
`Roles`, `ROLE_RANK`, `DEFAULT_ROLE` and the free `isRole`, `highestRank` and `canAssignRole` are removed, not deprecated.
The type is the sidebar's top tier, above the domain.

title: An entity can declare a hierarchy
readWhen: an entity's records nest under one another (categories, folders, accounts and their branches), building breadcrumbs or a tree from records, or about to write a recursive query — one member marks the parent, the tree is built in memory from the records already loaded, and a parent member must travel over the wire
summary:
An id, not a `link`.
two parent members. Two would be two trees over the same records, and which one a table indents by would depend on declaration order.
a parent that is not an `id` or a `string`.
a parent that is `hidden` or `readonly`.
No recursive query, no materialized path, no `$graphLookup`.

title: A unit of work the outbox, inbox and command claim join
readWhen: a write has to announce itself on the bus, a consumer has to fold a message exactly once, or a participant has to answer a redelivered command with what it decided the first time — and you are about to open a driver session by hand to make two of those one fact
summary:
`committed` — the writes, the events and the claim are durable.
`duplicate` — the claim was already taken.
`aborted` — the body failed with a business reason.

title: Entity routes are derived, and the repository comes from context
readWhen: writing a list, read, create, update or delete route for an entity, a route's links name a verb that answers `404`, or a route builds its own repository from a database handle
summary:
`verbs` — which exist.
`guard` — `public`, `permission`, `organization`, or `crossing` with or without a caller-named organization; one for every verb or split by read and write.
`scope` — which records a reader sees, as a filter conjoined onto the parsed request (never substituted, so no `or` in a query can widen it) plus a predicate…
`prepare` — what a save must pass, able to change the record or refuse it with a status and a code.

title: `like` ignores accents
readWhen: a search for `cafe` does not find `Café`, writing a filter translator for a new engine, or about to add a collation, a text index or a second "search" operator
summary:
`like` and `nlike` match with accents and case ignored, in every engine, by one rule.
In memory folds both sides and compares (`containsFolded`).
Mongo cannot fold the stored value in a `find`, so it widens the query: the search is folded and each letter becomes the class of its accented forms…
SQL folds the column with the built-in `translate(column, from, to)` and compares with `ILIKE` against the folded search (`FOLD_TRANSLATION`).

title: Facet counts are a port of their own
readWhen: a listing has to show how many records each filter choice would keep ("Aurora (12)"), adding a count or an aggregation to a store, or about to put counts on `EntityPage` or a method on `EntityRepository`
summary:
Counting is its own port, `EntityFacetCounter`, beside the repository and never part of it.
`count(queries)` takes one `EntityFacetQuery` per member, `{ member, filtering }`, and answers the values each member holds and how many records hold each one.
It is opened per request by `EntityFacetCounterFactoryTag`, as the repository is by `EntityRepositoryFactoryTag` (ADR 0010), with the same refusal of a…
`makeEntityFacetRoutes` mounts `GET <entity>/$facets` beside, not inside, `makeEntityRoutes`.
The wire is a repeated `facet=<member>` with each facet's filtering as RSQL under `rsql.<member>`, parsed against the entity's metadata.

title: Failures are typed values with a family and a category, and the shell decides what they mean
readWhen: adding a refusal or an error type, mapping a failure to an HTTP status, writing an error body by hand, catching an adapter's error with `instanceof`, deciding whether a bus message is poison, or about to call `Effect.log*` from a package that is not a shell
summary:
`_tag` — what happened, open-ended (`DuplicateSlug`, `CardDeclined`).
`code` — the permanent, wire-visible key a client translates.
`category` — one of a closed set, below.
`family` — derived from the category, never declared.
business — _an answer_.

title: Retry once, at the layer directly above the failure, under a budget and a deadline
readWhen: adding a retry, a backoff or a `Schedule` to a call, sizing a queue's `maxAttempts`, an outage gets worse when its dependency comes back, a request keeps working after its caller gave up, or about to retry inside a bus consumer
summary:
A coordinator retries a participant.
A bus consumer's only retry is redelivery.
The browser does not retry.
a call not marked idempotent — retrying a non-idempotent write is a second write.
a predicate that admits the business family — a type error, and a runtime guard behind it for predicates built dynamically.

title: Composed flows and use-case resolution: fragments, a pinned routing slip, ordered predicates over a verified context
readWhen: adding a step to a multi-step flow, letting a module contribute to a flow it does not own, choosing an implementation from who is calling, narrowing a read to its caller, or about to write a `SagaDefinition` or a `scope` callback
summary:
An endpoint router maps a path to a handler.
A use-case resolver maps a handler to an implementation, chosen from what is known about the caller.
Resolve from verified facts only.
Entitlement gates eligibility. A variant's `requires` is checked before its predicate; an unentitled variant is skipped, never chosen and then refused.
Nothing below the shell composes.

title: A flow engine port, and a durable workflow adapter that interprets the pinned slip
readWhen: running a multi-step flow, deciding where a flow survives its process dying, adding a wait, a child flow or a join to a flow, bumping the `effect` pin, or about to import `effect/workflow` or `effect/cluster`
summary:
`start(slip, idempotencyKey) → { flowId }`, idempotent on the key;.
`status(flowId)`, `signal(flowId, token, outcome)`, `interrupt(flowId)`;.
`signalCorrelated(correlation, { outcome, … })`, for a sender that knows what a wait is correlated with — the order a delivery follows — and neither the flow…
typed failures.
`effect/workflow` and `effect/cluster` are imported nowhere else.

title: Circuit breaker and bulkhead ports, with per-process engines
readWhen: a failing dependency drags down its callers, a consumer quarantines messages during an outage, sizing how many concurrent calls a participant may take, or about to write a breaker or a semaphore by hand
summary:
`CircuitBreakerTag` — `guard(key)(effect)` and the state for a key;.
`BulkheadTag` — `withPermit(key)(effect)`.

title: One outbox for every domain event, ordered per aggregate
readWhen: emitting a domain event from a write, consuming an event that may arrive out of order, an event stuck at the head of the outbox delays unrelated ones, writing an outbox on a new engine, or about to reach for change data capture
summary:
`eventId` — still the unique dedup key;.
`aggregate { type, id }` — what the event is about;.
`version` — that aggregate's version the event describes;.

title: The envelope is a Schema codec over an open message registry
readWhen: reading or writing an envelope on HTTP, the bus or the stream, adding a message type or a domain event, deciding who may receive a message, or about to cast a parsed body to its type
summary:
`meta.version` is required on every message that bears an entity: the aggregate version it describes, the one ADR 0018's consumers discard older versions by.
`meta.audience` is `{ kind: 'organization' | 'party' | 'flow', id, digest? }[]`.
An asynchronous failure carried in `data` uses the problem encoding of ADR 0013, with `code` and `category`.

title: Endpoints are Schema descriptors, and the service shell builds an HttpApi
readWhen: adding a route to a service, guarding one, writing an error body or a status by hand, building a link to a verb, a client decoding an error by its status, or about to import `effect/http` or `effect/http-api` outside the service shell
summary:
`errors` admits only `EntifixFailure` classes (ADR 0013), so a refusal that has no category does not compile.
`implement(descriptor, handler)` types the handler from the descriptor.
A descriptor carries no status, content type or HTTP annotation, so core never depends on `effect/http*`.
A payload is JSON unless it says otherwise.
`binaryBody({ contentTypes, maxBytes })` is raw bytes — a receipt, a photo — not base64 in JSON, which costs a third more.

title: Server push is a port, served over one multiplexed stream per tab
readWhen: pushing anything from a service to a browser, opening a second `EventSource` in one tab, a stream dies when its token expires, a fleet restart makes every browser reconnect at once, deciding who may receive a pushed event, or about to add a control endpoint or a WebSocket beside the stream
summary:
Server: `ServerPushTag`, at `@entifix/service-shell/push`, with the SSE adapter at `@entifix/service-shell/push/sse`.
Client: `PushChannelTag`, in `@entifix/react-integration`, with its `EventSource` adapter at `/event-source`.
Commands stay HTTP. The stream is one-way.
The push port is a subpath, not part of `.`.
A tab holds one `EventSource` per base URL and multiplexes every topic over it.

title: One mutation API, two settle modes, and a pending-flow store
readWhen: a write answers `202`, building an optimistic update, a pending state has to survive a reload, a flow's failure has to reach the user, showing money as taken before it is, or about to poll a status route from the browser
summary:
`Settled<T>` on `200` or `201`: the write happened, and the body is the entity.
`Pending` on `202`: the body decodes as `flowAccepted`.
`WriteResult<T>`, `Settled<T>` and `Pending` live in core, so a port can name them.
`buildEntityRestAdapterWrite` is a screen's save and delete over REST, and sends an update as `PUT` or `PATCH` by the `update` option.
The repository's `save` keeps answering the stored entity, because the Mongo and SQL adapters share that port and a pending write has no entity to return.

title: Change Validation, and what may trust the cache it carries
readWhen: a CI job is slow because it rebuilds what another job built, adding a job or a check to `change_validation.yml`, a check passed without running, the Actions cache is near its 10 GB, or about to restore `.nx/cache` between runners — a restored `.nx/cache` is ignored by Nx 24, and a repository-wide assertion must never read from the cache
summary:
The repository assertions (`@entifix/tiers`, `@entifix/docs-check`).
The workflow engine's chaos suite.
Publishing. `release.yml`'s publish job installs and builds from source on a fresh runner, and nothing restores a cache into it.

title: WCAG 2.2 AA is the target, and the gates ratchet toward it
readWhen: a control fails an accessibility check, adding a component or a story, a story renders blank while `build-storybook` stays green, writing an e2e journey that a screen-level check should cover, or about to add an axe rule exception, a jsx-a11y suppression or a `'todo'` entry
summary:
Every component and organism in `@entifix/react-controls`, and every shell surface in `@entifix/next-shell`, conforms to WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
`.storybook/main.ts` runs the same `unplugin-swc` pass (`decoratorVersion: '2022-03'`) that `vitest.shared.mts` uses.
Every `ui/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<name>/` folder carries a `*.stories.tsx`.
Every link and button a story renders has a name in the accessibility tree Playwright computes in Chromium (`.storybook/gate-browser.vitest.ts`), which is what…
Addons. `@storybook/addon-a11y` and `@storybook/addon-vitest` are devDependencies of `@entifix/react-controls`.

title: The token contract: contrast pairs, control borders, target size, and names that cannot collide
readWhen: adding or changing a palette or a preset, a host registers a runtime `ThemePalette`, a control is hard to see at rest or when focused, a menu item or option shows no active state, a target is under 24px at compact density, a dialog or palette renders a few pixels wide, or about to write a Tailwind arbitrary value or a colour literal
summary:
`--color-border` stays decorative — dividers, card edges — and may stay subtle.
`--color-selected` marks a selected-but-not-focused item (a chosen row, a current option).
An active descendant — a menu item, a palette option or a combobox option under the keyboard — wears `focus-ring` on `[data-focus]`, which the utility already…
`--color-{success,warning,info}`, each with `-subtle` and `-content`,.
`--color-scrim` for overlay backdrops, and a `--z-*` scale — `dropdown`, `sticky`, `overlay`, `toast`, `palette` — replacing literals.

title: Actions: one primary, an overflow, and a destructive verb that declares how it is undone
readWhen: adding a verb to an entity, a screen shows a row of equal-weight buttons, a delete or cancel happens in one click, "New" appears where nothing can be created, a toolbar or bulk verb acts on every matching row, a Server Action needs a confirmation without JavaScript, or about to add a keyboard shortcut
summary:
One component. `<ActionBar surface actions>` replaces the per-surface limits in EntityForm, EntityTable and BulkActionBar.
What shows. - The primary. - Up to three secondaries, in declaration and `priority` order. - Then a "More actions" menu button: the WAI-ARIA menu button…
Destructive placement. - A destructive verb is never primary on a page.
"New" on a list.
Every verb goes through `invoke()`.

title: The table evolves natively: header sort, container pivot, live counts, and no table engine yet
